topic: What 1% on a mortgage rate costs
hook: A single percent could cost you ninety-four grand.
visual_style: Photorealistic cinematic film still, real materials and textures, shallow depth of field, warm suburban golden-hour light, soft greens and warm brick, gold coins catching the sun

captions.hook_line: One percentage point on a $400k mortgage costs almost $95,000 🏡
captions.body: On a $400,000 30-year fixed loan, the principal-and-interest payment is about $2,398 at 6% and $2,661 at 7%: $263 more a month, about $94,700 more over the loan. Taxes and insurance are extra. Comparing Loan Estimates from several lenders is how buyers find a better rate. Education, not financial advice.
captions.comment_prompt: What rate did you get, or what are you seeing right now?

sources.claim: Shopping for a mortgage and comparing Loan Estimates
Standard amortization: $400,000 for 30 years is about $2,398 a month at 6% and $2,661 at 7%

blocks.narration: A single percent could cost you ninety-four grand. Here is the simple math, on a typical thirty-year home loan.

blocks.narration: At seven percent, it jumps to about twenty-six sixty. That is two hundred sixty-three dollars more, every single month.

blocks.narration: Stretch that over thirty years, and it adds up to roughly ninety-four thousand seven hundred dollars in extra interest.
